subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Year 10
syllabus: Victorian Curriculum F-10 Version 2.0: Mathematics, Level 10

points.title: Exact values and rounding errors
points.brief: Rounding a value early and using it again and again lets small errors grow, so keep exact values such as √2 or 1/3 until the end.

points.title: Taking out an algebraic common factor
points.brief: Take out the highest common factor including variables, such as 6x²y - 9xy = 3xy(2x - 3).

points.title: Index laws for algebraic products and quotients
points.brief: Simplify expressions such as (4a³b)(2ab²) = 8a⁴b³ and 12x⁵ ÷ 3x² = 4x³ by dealing with numbers and each variable in turn.

points.title: Adding and subtracting algebraic fractions
points.brief: Find a common denominator, rewrite each fraction, then combine the numerators, such as x/3 + x/4 = 7x/12.

points.title: Multiplying and dividing algebraic fractions
points.brief: Multiply straight across, or multiply by the reciprocal to divide, cancelling common factors before you multiply.

points.title: Changing the subject of a formula
points.brief: Use inverse operations to get one variable on its own, such as rearranging v = u + at to make a the subject.

points.title: Writing equations from word problems
points.brief: Name the unknown with a letter, write the facts as an equation, solve it, and check the answer makes sense in the situation.

points.title: Equations with algebraic fractions
points.brief: Multiply every term by the lowest common denominator to clear the fractions, then solve as usual.

points.title: Solving multi-step linear inequalities
points.brief: Solve like an equation, but reverse the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number.

points.title: Solving simultaneous equations with graphs
points.brief: The solution of two linear equations is the point where their lines cross. Parallel lines never cross, so there is no solution.

points.title: The substitution method
points.brief: Make one variable the subject of one equation and substitute it into the other, leaving one equation with one unknown.

points.title: The elimination method
points.brief: Add or subtract the equations, after multiplying one if needed, so that one variable cancels out.

points.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
points.brief: Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to -1, such as 2 and -1/2.

points.title: Factorising quadratics with a common factor first
points.brief: Take out any common factor before factorising the quadratic left inside, such as 2x² + 10x + 12 = 2(x + 2)(x + 3).

points.title: Solving quadratic equations by factorising
points.brief: Rearrange so one side is zero, factorise, then use the null factor law, such as x² - x = 6 giving x = 3 or x = -2.

points.title: Solving equations by guess, check and refine
points.brief: When algebra is hard, test values, see whether each is too high or too low, and narrow in on the solution, checking for more than one.

points.title: Recognising non-linear graphs
points.brief: The shapes of a parabola (y = x²), a hyperbola (y = 1/x), a circle (x² + y² = r²) and an exponential curve (y = 2ˣ), from their equations.

points.title: Solving simple exponential equations
points.brief: Write both sides as powers of the same base and set the indices equal, such as 2ˣ = 32 = 2⁵, so x = 5.

points.title: Compound interest
points.brief: Interest is added each period and then earns interest itself, so A = P(1 + r)ⁿ, growing faster than simple interest.

points.title: Exponential growth and decay
points.brief: A quantity that grows or shrinks by the same percentage each period, such as a population or a car's value, is multiplied by the same factor each time.

points.title: Inverse proportion
points.brief: When one quantity doubles and the other halves, they are inversely proportional, y = k/x, such as speed and travel time for a fixed trip.

points.title: Surface area of composite objects
points.brief: Add the areas of the faces that are on the outside, leaving out any faces hidden where two solids join.

points.title: Logarithmic scales
points.brief: On scales such as the Richter scale, decibels and pH, each step up of 1 means 10 times as much, not 1 more.

points.title: Angles of elevation and depression
points.brief: An angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal and an angle of depression down from it, and they form right-angled triangles to solve.

points.title: True bearings
points.brief: A true bearing is the angle measured clockwise from north, written with three digits, such as 045°T for north-east.

points.title: Writing a geometric proof
points.brief: A deductive proof moves from given facts to the result in steps, giving a known property or theorem as the reason for each step.

points.title: Using congruence in proofs
points.brief: Proving two triangles congruent shows that their matching sides and angles are equal, which proves other facts about a shape.

points.title: Networks, vertices and edges
points.brief: A network shows connections as vertices joined by edges, and the degree of a vertex is the number of edges meeting there.

points.title: Paths and connected networks
points.brief: A network is connected when there is a path between every pair of vertices, and paths model routes such as roads or deliveries.

points.title: Quartiles and interquartile range
points.brief: Quartiles split ordered data into four equal parts. The interquartile range, Q3 minus Q1, is the spread of the middle half.

points.title: Five-number summary and box plots
points.brief: The minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum are drawn as a box plot, which shows the centre, spread and shape at a glance.

points.title: Identifying outliers with the IQR
points.brief: A value more than 1.5 × IQR below Q1 or above Q3 counts as an outlier and is shown as a separate point.

points.title: Comparing data with parallel box plots
points.brief: Box plots on the same scale compare medians, IQRs and ranges, and show which group is higher or more spread out.

points.title: Scatterplots and association
points.brief: A scatterplot shows two numerical variables, and the association is described by its direction, strength and whether it is linear.

points.title: Lines of good fit
points.brief: A straight line drawn through the middle of the points to predict one variable from the other, more safely inside the data than beyond it.

points.title: Two-way tables for categorical variables
points.brief: Comparing row or column percentages in a two-way table shows whether two categorical variables seem related.

points.title: Time series data
points.brief: Data recorded over time, with time on the horizontal axis, read for trends, seasonal patterns and unusual points.

points.title: Judging statistical claims
points.brief: Check a claim against its data, its sample and its display, and watch for bias, and for correlation being sold as cause.

points.title: Three-step experiments
points.brief: Extend a tree diagram to three steps, such as three coin tosses, and multiply along the branches for each outcome.

points.title: Independent events
points.brief: Events are independent when one does not change the other's probability, and then P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).

points.title: Conditional probability
points.brief: The probability of A given B counts only the outcomes where B happened, so the sample space shrinks to B.

points.title: Conditional probability from a two-way table
points.brief: To find a probability given a condition, use only the row or column for that condition as the total.
